_provenance.note: LLM reading of the lens token tables; not a measurement

axes.label: formal news reporting ↔ casual personal chat
axes.rationale: Negative ends across Jacobian, logit and real correlations show newswire tokens (Reuters, spokesman/spokeswoman, Officials, President, Tuesday, Advertisement), while positive ends show second-person and slang tokens (you, your, kinda, alot, youre, haha, lol, Awesome).

axes.label: sentence-initial contrastive connectives ↔ mid-clause function words
axes.rationale: Negative ends of the Jacobian, tuned and real-correlation readouts consistently show discourse connectives (but, But, Yet, However, Although, While, whereas). The real-correlation positive end shows mid-sentence prepositions and conjunctions (on, is, to, with, for), while the lens positives are subword noise.

axes.label: chatty/political commentary ↔ instructional documentation
axes.rationale: The Jacobian positive end (Instructions, Requirements, Description, Examples, Types) and the real-correlation positive end (Select, Consult, Apply, Download, Choose) point to manual-style imperative text. The negative ends show emoticon and ellipsis punctuation (:), !!, ...) and political speech reporting (said, Oh, Obama, Hillary). The logit and tuned lenses are mostly noise.
